title: `rechunk()` sometimes lead to arrays with non-regular chunks (`dask==2025.1.0`)
body:
**Describe the issue**:

Rechunking with `'auto'` sometimes lead to arrays whose chunks are not regular, making `dask.array.to_zarr()` fail (the validation `_check_regular_chunks()` from `dask.array.core` fails. This is shown in the example below. Passing explicit chunk dimensions instead of `'auto'` fixes the problem. Bug reproducible with `dask==2025.1.0`.

Related to: https://github.com/dask/dask/issues/11544. The bug was originally reported from @participant3 in the context of the [spatialdata package](https://github.com/scverse/spatialdata/issues/821). I kept the dimensionalities of the original bug report in the code example below.

**Minimal Complete Verifiable Example**:
```python
import dask.array as da
from dask.array.core import _check_regular_chunks
import pytest


# Function to create a lazy zero-filled dask array
def create_lazy_zeros(shape, chunks, dtype='uint16'):
    return da.zeros(shape, chunks=chunks, dtype=dtype)


# Create the mock array with lazy zeros
def create_mock_array():
    # Define the shape and chunks for scale0
    shape = (1, 25778, 35416)
    chunks = (1, 4096, 4096)

    # Create a lazy zero-filled dask array
    data = create_lazy_zeros(shape, chunks)

    return data


# Create the mock array
mock_array = create_mock_array()

# Slice the array
sliced_array = mock_array[:, :13000, 15000:35000]
print('Chunks before rechunking')
print(sliced_array.chunks)

# Rechunk the array with 'auto'
sliced_array_auto = sliced_array.rechunk('auto')
print('Chunks after rechunking with auto')
print(sliced_array_auto.chunks)

# Check for regular chunks
with pytest.raises(AssertionError):
    assert _check_regular_chunks(sliced_array_auto.chunks)

# Rechunk the array with a fixed chunk size
FIXED_CHUNK = 4096
sliced_array_fixed = sliced_array.rechunk((1, FIXED_CHUNK, FIXED_CHUNK))
print(f'Chunks after rechunking with a fixed chunk size (FIXED_CHUNK)')
print(sliced_array_fixed.chunks)

# Assert that chunks are regular
assert _check_regular_chunks(sliced_array_fixed.chunks)
```

**Anything else we need to know?**:

**Environment**:

- Dask version: 2025.1.0
- Python version: 3.11.0
- Operating System: macOS 14.6.1
- Install method (conda, pip, source): conda (`conda-forge`)

comments.author: participant2
comments.body: Deviating from regular chunks was an intentional decision to improve efficiency of computations. So that part works as expected. I agree though that the default experience when writing to zarr should be better and just work through injecting a rechunk to get the required chunking

comments.author: reporter
comments.body: Thank you for your comment. What I find confusing is that calling `sliced_array.rechunk('auto')` seems to have no effects. I think it could be made cleared that the new default behavior for `'auto'` is to keep the chunks irregular.

comments.author: participant2
comments.body:
Do you have a reproducer that is actually hitting this error?

```
        if not _check_regular_chunks(arr.chunks):
            # We almost certainly get here because auto chunking has been used
            # on irregular chunks. The max will then be smaller than auto, so using
            # max is a safe choice
            arr = arr.rechunk(tuple(map(max, arr.chunks)))
```

this should protect against the problem you are seeing

comments.author: reporter
comments.body: Yes, I implemented a workaround here https://github.com/scverse/spatialdata/pull/861/files, I could use the code you suggest instead. In this way I don't have to hardcode (or have the user decide): `CHUNK_SIZE = 1024`.

comments.author: reporter
comments.body: I tracked this task here https://github.com/scverse/spatialdata/issues/872 (not urgent). Meanwhile if you think your approach is enough, I think this issue can be closed. Thanks again!

comments.author: participant2
comments.body: Yeah I saw this, but do you have a unit test or something similar that explains how you got to this exception? I'd like to fix this in Dask itself so that you don't have to handle this in your library

comments.author: reporter
comments.body:
Ah got it. The real code triggering this was case basically the one that I posted as first post, with the exception of replacing `_check_regular_chunks(sliced_array_auto.chunks)` with `sliced_array_auto.to_zarr()`.

I'll make a snippet now, simplifying the code above.

comments.author: reporter
comments.body:
Here is it:

```python
import dask.array as da
from tempfile import TemporaryDirectory


shape = (1, 25778, 35416)
chunks = (1, 4096, 4096)
mock_array = da.zeros(shape, chunks=chunks, dtype="uint16")
sliced_array = mock_array[:, :13000, 15000:35000]
sliced_array_auto = sliced_array.rechunk("auto")

with TemporaryDirectory() as tmpdir:
    sliced_array_auto.to_zarr(tmpdir)
```

comments.author: participant2
comments.body: This completes for me without raising because the rechunk we added in Dask hits and smoothes out the chunks. Does this raise for you? If yes, I'd be curious about the traceback

comments.author: participant2
comments.body: Any chance you are on 2024.11.2? I think we had one release without this automatic rechunking functionality.

comments.author: reporter
comments.body:
Good point! My first code snipped (the one using 
```python
with pytest.raises(AssertionError):
    assert _check_regular_chunks(sliced_array_auto.chunks)
```
fails with `2025.1.0`. Instead, the one using `to_zarr()` works on `2025.1.0`. I could not try the real world example on `2025.1.0` because `spatialdata` does not support the latest `dask` (due to the `.attrs` missing).

So it seems that no further changes on the dask size for this bug are needed. Wdyt?

comments.author: participant2
comments.body: Yes, correct. I think the bug has been fixed in 2024.12.0. I am closing this one
